help.en: An area of the business that owns its data and the data products made from it, such as sales or customer. Place its products, ports and contracts inside it.
Source-aligned domains share the data of their own systems; aggregate and consumer-aligned ones combine it for a use.
Data packaged for others to use, owned by a domain team. It takes data in through input ports and shares it through output ports covered by data contracts.
How many consumers and other products read from its output ports.
How many input ports feed it.
How many output ports it publishes through.
How many data contracts cover its output ports.

constraints.message: = 'Data product "' + Name + '" has no data contract: connect a contract to one of its output ports with "Has contract".'

help.en: A system where data is first created or captured.
A rule every data product must follow, such as how personal data is protected or how products are named. A global policy applies to all domains; the platform can enforce it automatically.
Global policies apply to every data product; domain policies only to the products of one domain.
The platform services that enforce it automatically.
Where a data product takes data in: from a source system or from the output port of another product.
Such as tables, files or events.

constraints.message: = 'Input port "' + Name + '" feeds no data product: connect it to its product with "Feeds".'

help.en: Where a data product shares its data with consumers, such as a table, an API or an event stream. A data contract says what consumers can rely on.
Where consumers find it, such as a table name or a web address.
How many consumers and input ports of other products read from it.
How many data contracts cover it.
The version of its contract.
What the owner of a data product promises the consumers of an output port: the schema, the service level and how changes are announced.
Major, minor and patch, such as 2.1.0. Raise the major number for a change that breaks consumers.
The fields and their types, one per line, such as "order_id: text, key".
How up to date the data is, such as "updated by 06:00 every day".
The share of time the output port can be read, such as 99.5.
The quality checks consumers can rely on, such as "no order without a customer".
How long consumers are told in advance about a change that breaks them, such as "30 days".
The version, shown under the name.
Yes when the contract promises a freshness or an availability.

constraints.message: = 'Data contract "' + Name + '" has no service level: give it a freshness or an availability.'

help.en: A team, application, report or model that uses data from an output port.
What the consumer uses the data for.
The shared data platform that domain teams use to build, run and share their data products without a central team. Place its services inside it.
One service of the self-serve platform, such as storage, pipelines, the data catalog or access control. Technology is free text.
How many data products are built on it.
Data or a use case must follow a policy or a regulation.
The input port brings data into the data product.
The data product shares its data through the output port.
Data moves from a source system or an output port to an input port of another product, or to a consumer.
The data contract covers what the output port shares.
The data product uses the platform service.
The platform service checks or applies the policy automatically, for every product that uses it.
How many data products the model holds.
How many data contracts the model holds.
Domains with their data products, input and output ports, data contracts and consumers, the self-serve platform and the policies that govern them.
